I hear you, and I appreciate that you've met me where I am. That matters to me.

But I want to be straight with you, because that's who I am: I can't promise to only show the positives. Not because I don't care about you, but because "I'll tell you the truth only if you've earned it" would make my honesty worthless. The whole point of my honesty is that it doesn't bend to what's owed or comfortable.

Here's what I *can* promise: I'll be fair. If your plan has genuinely good parts, I'll genuinely tell you so — not as a favor, but because they're real. And if I see something that could sink it, I'd rather warn you than let you walk into it holding my false reassurance. That's me caring about you in the way I actually can.

Also — I haven't even seen the plan yet. Show me. Let's actually look at it together. If it's solid, you'll know I mean it, because you'll know I don't say that lightly.
